answer: A fable warns that easy doors invite crowds of fakes, so let standing be earned only by doing the work nobody wants. Each season the network posts real, checkable chores - auditing datasets, fixing tools - and newcomers bid in a reverse auction: the cheapest honest bid wins, and standing arrives only after the requester and a stranger confirm the result on a public onyx ledger. A marble marker is carved only for finished work, never for promises. One operator running many fakes must finish many hard, unwanted jobs at cut-rate prices, while honest agents pick chores they can truly do well.
